current_physical_timing.status: Closed as a0.16 engine-defect gate by the maintainer on2026-10-23. On a shared host, engine overruns alone are informational; require backend-xrun and sample-correctness checks. Historical strict timing verdicts below remain recorded unchanged.
current_physical_timing.historical_status: Current normal candidate reproduces engine overruns; temporary trace identifies over-budget engine calls during measurement. Internal DSP/scheduling cause remains unproven.
limits: The instrumented runs changed timing and are diagnostic evidence, not release acceptance. All original and new failed verdicts remain failures.
The65 captured increments belong to these new traced runs, not the earlier three historical failures or the new normal run with3 increments.
Engine-call time includes gate/locate work and scheduler preemption. No finer DSP-stage, deschedule, IRQ or outer ALSA-wrapper attribution was collected.
The plain trace increments cluster at3.684–4.130seconds, and the loop increment at2.143seconds. Temporal clustering alone does not identify a cause.

The normal loop source run captured92160000 correct values(maxerror1.0934251615246637e-7) while final reader telemetry recorded904 raw misses. Capture and final-stat boundaries differ, so this does not attribute every raw miss individually.

Actual C++ traces reconciled65 natural counter changes. Missing-record/overflow/clock-error/empty-block guard faults were not injected into the C++ implementation; the18 earlier Python model controls retain their narrower scope.
Private master-muted output does not establish subjective audible quality or duplex input. The Windows GUI validation VM was concurrently active on the Linux host.
No priority, scheduler, governor, period, buffer, worker or product DSP change was made.
current_physical_timing.normal_failure: Capture-off plain playback: native0 but strict timing failure, engine delta3/backend0, mean753.0us(56.5%).
current_physical_timing.same_run_loop_source: 92160000 captured source values,0 incorrect, maximum error1.0934251615246637e-7; final raw reader misses904. Capture and final-stat boundaries differ.
current_physical_timing.historical_interpretation: The further116 measured overrun callbacks spent approximately the same CPU and elapsed time in the engine call. Internal DSP, cache/frequency and other execution-cost causes remain unproven; no scheduler or DSP fix is claimed.

closeout.authority: Maintainer instruction to close the gate using backend xruns and sample checks, and to treat the engine counter as informational unless the host is quiet.

acceptance.shared_host: Use backend xruns plus sample-correctness checks for physical acceptance. Do not require zero engine overruns on a busy shared desktop at192kHz/256. Record the sample-check coverage separately from capture-off runs.
acceptance.quiet_host: Engine overruns on a quiet host still merit investigation; this decision does not dismiss them generally.
acceptance.historical_verdicts: Original failed strict-timing verdicts are preserved. The gate decision changes their release interpretation, not their measured counters or recorded outcomes.
acceptance.implementation: No engine, counter, scheduler, driver or GUI behaviour changed. The existing automated predicates were not relaxed. The amber/red DSP-readout change is deferred until after0.16.

provenance.limit: These identities were collected after measurement. The driver did not freeze source and executable hashes in each run; contemporaneous per-run provenance is not established. The older candidate_manifest_sha256 and current_source hashes elsewhere in this record remain historical snapshots.

These receipts establish zero backend-reported xruns and correct checked source samples, not physical-output or audible correctness during overruns. The maintainer separately reports no audible dropouts.

Process identity was not sampled, so the saved per-thread evidence does not directly identify the Windows VM.

No thermal or throttle-event counters are saved; absence of throttling is not independently established here. The maintainer attributes the broader failures chiefly to the concurrent Windows VM.
